title: AgainstTheGrain: reversal depends on the substrate
summary: AgainstTheGrain takes the Geometric Neuron direction machinery and asks a deliberately backward question: what changes when a computation learned in one temporal direction is driven in reverse? The strongest surviving result is not that reverse is universally expensive, but that reversal cost depends on the representation. A worn dissipative sequence can be ill-conditioned backward while a coordinate manifold can reverse nearly freely. The pass preserves that correction and the negative controls that prevent direction from being read out of passive geometry or a scalar level alone.

nodes.claim: Turns the skew-lag/direction line around and measures what happens when a forward-built sequence model, predictor and timing gate are driven against their learned arrow, then compares that reversal with a coordinate representation that has no preferred direction.
nodes.survived: In the repo's seeded toy systems the skew half changes sign under reversal while the symmetric half is preserved; a smooth forward-trained predictor can become actively harmful on the reversed trajectory; and a dissipative worn sequence amplifies a small turnaround perturbation dramatically while a toroidal coordinate manifold keeps the same perturbation small. The durable abstraction is therefore substrate-dependent reversibility rather than reverse being intrinsically costly.
nodes.killed: Passive cable geometry plus a simple sigmoid does not generate the direction preference; a level-keyed gate cannot read the sign of acceleration; and the claim that any forward predictor poisons any reversed stream fails on unrelated states, where the predictor is approximately neutral. The biological habit/grid interpretation remains a bet rather than an identified mechanism.

edges.why: AgainstTheGrain explicitly lists GeometricNeuron V9's skew lag operator as the source of the result that the arrow lives in the antisymmetric half, then tests what that object does under reversal.
The repository explicitly lists GeometricNeuron V20's arrow-cost/recomposition line among its direct sources and turns those retained direction mechanisms into a dedicated reversal audit.

motifs.title: Reversal cost belongs to the representation, not to the word backward
motifs.description: AgainstTheGrain separates two substrates for the same nominal round trip: a dissipative learned sequence has a preferred arrow and can become unstable when inverted, while a coordinate manifold can represent the reverse direction without inverting the whole forward dynamics. The lesson complements MovingProblem's coordinate-history warning and the GeometricNeuron skew-operator line without claiming the toy substrates are identified biological circuits.
